what_it_does: Chip designers write rules called assertions — formal checks that say 'this signal must always be high before that one goes low' — and when a simulation breaks one of those rules, figuring out why is slow, expert-heavy work. This paper describes AssertSolver, an AI language model fine-tuned specifically to read an assertion failure report and suggest what went wrong in the chip blueprint (written in a hardware description language called SystemVerilog). The model was trained on thousands of synthetic examples pairing a broken assertion with the correct fix, and it also learns from its own mistakes by studying the error messages its earlier attempts produced. The result is an automated assistant that can propose fixes to hardware description bugs that previously required a specialist to unravel, though the claims here come from the abstract alone.
